title: three-maze/link v1: shared definitions
description: Value types every message schema uses (SPEC.md section 4). Every string is an enum, a constant or one of the patterned types below, so no file path and no .py name can travel in a message.
$comment: Patterns end in (?![\s\S]) instead of $ because Python's re lets $ match before a final newline, and the Python validator must reject what Ajv rejects. NOPY, the lookahead (?![\s\S]*\.[Pp][Yy][CcDdOoWw]?(?![A-Za-z0-9_])) after ^, rejects .py, .pyc, .pyd, .pyo and .pyw names in any letter case.

id.title: Id
id.description: Identifier of a world, zone, spawn, asset, experiment or software component: the scene-file id grammar. No slash, no backslash, no .py name.

request_id.title: RequestId
request_id.description: The id of a request and the re of its reply: chosen by the requester, unique among its open requests on one connection.

session_id.title: SessionId
session_id.description: Opaque session name chosen by the rig runtime, for example 2026-10-23T14-03-11Z_m12. It is a name, not a folder: the runtime alone maps it to files.

device_id.title: DeviceId
device_id.description: A device's own id as its hello line reports it (device protocol v1, section 4.1).

software_version.title: SoftwareVersion
software_version.description: Version of a program or library as it reports itself, for example 0.169.0, 44.7.0 or 152.0.7444.59.

token.title: Token
token.description: 128-bit session token as 32 lower-case hexadecimal digits (reserved; checked from DPR-16a on).

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: SHA-256 digest as 64 lower-case hexadecimal digits.

pointer.title: Pointer
pointer.description: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into a message, for example /data/samples/3/seq. Segments are property names or array indices; no dot, colon or backslash, so a file path cannot pass as a pointer.

text.title: Text
text.description: Short human-readable text in one line: no control characters (U+0000 to U+001F, U+007F to U+009F), no line or paragraph separator (U+2028, U+2029), no slash and no backslash (so no path or URL), no .py name.

time_us.title: TimeUs
time_us.description: A time in whole microseconds on a monotonic clock: perf_counter_ns() // 1000 in the rig runtime, Math.round(performance.now() * 1000) in JavaScript, the unwrapped device clock for t_dev_us. Never a wall-clock time.

message_time.title: MessageTime
message_time.description: The envelope's t: when the sender sent the message, on the sender's own monotonic clock.

count.title: Count
count.description: A non-negative integer that JSON carries exactly in every language (at most 2^53 - 1).

seq.title: Seq
seq.description: Device-sample sequence number: uint32, wrapping from 4294967295 to 0 (device protocol v1, D3 and section 7.2).

epoch.title: Epoch
epoch.description: Teleport and reset counter (ADR-0002, Motion worker): 0 at session start, +1 at every teleport or reset the motion worker applies.

world.title: WorldId
world.description: Id of the world a record belongs to. Phase 1 sessions have exactly one world; the field is there so that world switching (phase 2) needs no new field (plan item TS-09).

versions.title: Versions
versions.description: Versions of the components a client runs, by component id, for example {"electron": "44.7.0", "three": "0.169.0", "rapier3d-compat": "0.14.0"} (the session record keeps them, plan item DPR-08a).

motion_device.title: MotionDevice
motion_device.description: The motion device's profile and guarantee level, as the session record states them (device protocol v1, sections 8.2 and 8.3).

profile.description: How the runtime reads the device: v1 or legacy-v0.3.

completeness.description: What the session can claim about lost samples.

integrity.description: What the session can claim about corrupted samples.

seq_source.description: Who numbered the samples: the device, or the runtime as they arrived.

time_source.description: Whose clock t_dev_us is: the device's, or the runtime's at receipt.

n_axes.description: Number of raw count axes per sample.

device_id.description: The device's own id, when its hello line gave one.
